newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower in small-cap dominated market.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower in small-cap dominated market.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended lower as institutional investors gave way to local speculators who kept select small-capitalised issues very active.
The benchamrk Composite Index closed 4.27 points, or 0.39 percent, lower at 1,080.61, while the small-capitalised second Board index shed 1.75 points, or 0.31 percent, at 564.73.
"It's mainly second- and third-liners that are active today," said Mohaiyani Securities dealer Jonathan Duckett.
Shares of Malaysian International Shipping Corporation gained 20 cents to 7.20 ringgit on renewed rumours of a change in its shareholding structure.
"The rumours are that Mirzan is buying into MISC," said a research manager at a foreign brokerage.

Mirzan Mahathir controls transport and shipping firms Diperdana and Konsortium. Konosrtium has been rumoured to be eyeing a 30 percent stake in MISC, the national shipping company, currently owned by the Employees Provident Fund.

Meanwhile Transmile Air, an air transport company, also controlled by Mirzan, gained 1.10 ringgit to 18.10 ringgit, also on the MISC rumours. But some analysts said the rise was a purely speculative play, not connected with MISC.
